summary: South Korea admits citizens of over 100 countries without a visa for 30–180 days, normally subject to the K-ETA electronic travel authorization (10,000 KRW, valid 3 years) — though K-ETA has been temporarily waived for 22 countries including the US, UK and Japan; other nationalities apply for a C-3 short-term visit visa at an embassy.

fee.notes: About 7 USD, paid online by card. Not a visa — an electronic travel authorization for visa-free nationals. Temporarily waived for 22 countries; check the official site for the current waiver list.
Single entry up to 90 days about 40 USD; multiple-entry visas cost more (about 90 USD). Fees are collected in local currency and vary slightly by mission.

source.name: Korea Visa Portal — visa types and fees

passportValidity.text: Korea does not publish a strict 6-month rule: your passport must be valid for your entire stay, but at least 6 months of validity is recommended and airlines may apply stricter checks.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical coverage is recommended — Korean healthcare is excellent and foreigners pay in full.

onwardTicket.text: Visa-free and K-ETA travelers may be asked to show an onward or return ticket; airlines routinely check before boarding.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published, but immigration officers may ask about your itinerary, accommodation and means of support.

declarations.name: e-Arrival Card
declarations.text: Korea's free electronic arrival card can be submitted online within 3 days before arrival, replacing the paper arrival card (K-ETA holders and registered foreign residents are already exempt from the arrival card). A customs declaration is only needed if you have goods to declare.

currencyLimits.text: Currency and monetary instruments exceeding 10,000 USD in total (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

notes: Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes, 2 bottles of alcohol (up to 2 liters total, under 400 USD) and goods worth up to 800 USD per adult.
Fresh fruit, meat and many agricultural products cannot be brought in — fines for undeclared items are heavy.

payments.text: Credit and debit cards are accepted almost everywhere, including taxis and street markets. A rechargeable T-money card covers subways, buses and convenience stores nationwide. Cash is rarely needed but useful at traditional markets.

safety.text: South Korea is one of the safest destinations in the world, with very low street crime. Follow civil-emergency guidance during occasional North Korea-related drills.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — South Korea Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring (April–May, cherry blossoms) and fall (September–November, foliage) are the most pleasant; summer is hot, humid and rainy, and winters are cold but clear.

idp.text: South Korea is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Geneva, 1949), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3)

driving.text: South Korea is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for South Korea yet.

tips.text: Check whether your passport currently needs a K-ETA before booking — the waiver for 22 countries was announced only through the end of 2025, and requirements can be reinstated. Apply only at k-eta.go.kr (10,000 KRW); third-party sites charge large mark-ups.
Buy a T-money card at any convenience store on arrival — it works on subways, buses and taxis nationwide and can pay at convenience stores too.
Google Maps navigation is limited in Korea — download Naver Map or Kakao Map (both have English versions) for directions and public transport.
Fill in the free e-Arrival Card online (e-arrivalcard.go.kr) within 3 days before arrival to skip the paper form at immigration.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa or K-ETA for South Korea?
faq.answer: US citizens do not need a visa for stays up to 90 days. A K-ETA is normally required, but it was temporarily waived for US passport holders (along with 21 other countries) through the end of 2025. Whether the waiver continues in 2026 has not been confirmed — check k-eta.go.kr shortly before travel.

faq.question: What is the K-ETA and how much does it cost?
faq.answer: The Korea Electronic Travel Authorization is an online pre-clearance for visa-free visitors, costing 10,000 KRW (about 7 USD) and valid for 3 years for multiple visits. Apply at k-eta.go.kr at least 72 hours before boarding. K-ETA holders also skip the arrival card at immigration.

faq.question: How long can Canadians stay in South Korea?
faq.answer: Canadian citizens get the longest visa-free stay Korea offers — up to 180 days — under the bilateral arrangement. The K-ETA requirement was temporarily waived for Canadians through the end of 2025; confirm the current status before flying.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens visit South Korea without a visa?
faq.answer: Individual Chinese travelers still need a C-3 short-term visit visa. Korea began a trial visa-free scheme for Chinese group tourists in late September 2025 (announced through June 2026), but it only covers organized tour groups — confirm current conditions with a Korean embassy or on visa.go.kr.

faq.question: How much does a South Korean tourist visa cost?
faq.answer: For nationalities that need one (including Indian, Filipino, Vietnamese and Indonesian citizens), the single-entry C-3 short-term visit visa costs about 40 USD for stays up to 90 days; multiple-entry visas cost about 90 USD. Apply through a Korean embassy or designated visa center — see visa.go.kr.
